learn.hook: Your mother cooks a delicious dinner and a restaurant chef cooks the same dish. Both are work, but one is paid. What's the difference?
points: Work done in return for money or payment in kind (like grain) is called an economic activity. Examples: a farmer selling vegetables, a teacher teaching, a tailor stitching clothes for customers.
Work done without payment, out of love, care, duty or to help others, is a non-economic activity. Examples: cooking for one's own family, caring for a sick grandparent, volunteering.
The same task can be economic or non-economic: a cook in a hotel is paid, while cooking for one's own family at home is not paid.
Unpaid work at home, like cooking, cleaning and caring, is very valuable. Families could not run without it, even though it earns no money.
Volunteering for the community, like helping at a community kitchen or a clean-up drive, is also valuable non-economic work.

example.q: Kavya's father works as a driver for a company in the day and drives his own mother to the hospital in the evening. Which is economic activity?
steps: Driving for the company earns him a salary, so it is economic activity.
Driving his mother is done out of care, without pay.
So the evening drive is non-economic activity.
example.answer: Driving for the company is economic; driving his mother is non-economic.

learn.reallife: Volunteers who serve food at a community kitchen, and grandparents who look after grandchildren, are doing valuable unpaid work.

It earns income in money or in kind.

options: Work done in return for money or payment in kind
quiz.explain: Economic activities earn income, such as a salary, wages or goods.

quiz.q: Which of these is a non-economic activity?
options: A doctor treating patients in a clinic
Caring for a sick grandparent at home
quiz.explain: Caring for family out of love is unpaid, so it is non-economic.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only paid work counts as work

quiz.q: A cook works in a hotel and is paid a salary. What kind of activity is this?
quiz.explain: The cook earns money for cooking, so it is an economic activity.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the task with whether it is paid

quiz.q: Why is unpaid work at home valuable?
options: It is done only on holidays
Families depend on it to run every day
quiz.explain: Cooking, cleaning and caring keep families healthy and happy even though they are not paid.

quiz.explain: Some workers, like farm labourers, may get grain or goods as payment.

quiz.q: Neha helps clean up a lake with a group of volunteers, without pay. What type of activity is this?
quiz.explain: Volunteering is done to help others, without pay, so it is non-economic.

quiz.q: Which pair shows the same task as both economic and non-economic?
options: A paid tutor teaching students, and an elder sister helping her brother study
quiz.explain: Teaching is economic when paid and non-economic when done for family.
quiz.mistake: Does not see that payment decides the type

quiz.q: Which of these is an economic activity?
options: A mother stitching a button on her own child's shirt
A tailor stitching a dress for a customer
quiz.explain: The tailor is paid by the customer, so it is economic.
quiz.mistake: Thinks stitching is always the same type of activity

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Is cooking at home work? Nobody pays for it!'
teach.praise: Oh! Paid work is economic activity, and unpaid work like cooking at home is non-economic, but it is just as valuable!
teach.nudge: What is the difference between paid and unpaid work? Is unpaid work valuable?

learn.hook: Imagine a city where sanitation workers stop for a week. Every job matters!
points: Dignity of labour means that every kind of honest work deserves respect, whether it is done with the hands or the mind.
Farmers, sanitation workers, cobblers, weavers, construction workers, doctors and engineers all keep society running.
No honest work is 'small'. Treating some jobs as low and others as high is unfair.
We show respect by thanking workers, speaking politely, paying fairly and not making extra mess for others to clean.
Many traditions in India value serving others through work, like sharing food in community kitchens where everyone, rich or poor, helps and eats together.

example.q: Rohit's classmate laughs at a boy whose father is a cobbler. What should Rohit say?
steps: A cobbler repairs shoes that people need every day.
His skill and honest work help many people.
Every honest job deserves respect, so laughing at it is unfair.
example.answer: That all honest work deserves respect: this is the dignity of labour.

learn.reallife: When you thank the school sweeper, the bus driver or the canteen staff, you are practising the dignity of labour.

games.title: Respect for work
items: Every honest job deserves respect.
That is the idea of dignity of labour.
Work done with the hands is less important than office work.
Both are needed; neither is less important.
Sanitation workers help keep us healthy.
Clean surroundings prevent many diseases.
Thanking workers is one way to show respect.
Polite words show that we value their work.
It is fine to mock someone because of their parent's job.
Mocking any honest work is unfair and hurtful.

options: Every kind of honest work deserves respect
Only highly paid jobs are important
quiz.explain: Dignity of labour means respecting all honest work equally.
quiz.mistake: Thinks only some jobs deserve respect

quiz.q: Which is a good way to show respect for workers?
quiz.explain: Kind words and good behaviour show we value their work.

quiz.q: Why are sanitation workers important to a city?
options: They keep the city clean and help prevent diseases
quiz.explain: Clean streets and drains keep everyone healthy.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the value of cleaning work

quiz.q: A classmate says, 'Farming is not a respectable job.' What is the best reply?
options: You are right, nobody needs farmers
Farmers grow our food; their work deserves great respect
quiz.explain: Without farmers we would have no food; their work is essential.

quiz.q: Which statement shows dignity of labour?
options: Some jobs are only for certain people
Only people with big offices matter
Every honest job, big or small, helps society
quiz.explain: All honest work is useful, so it should all be respected.
quiz.mistake: Holds the idea that some work is low

quiz.q: How can students practise dignity of labour at school?
options: By cleaning up after themselves and helping in class tasks
quiz.explain: Doing our share of work and respecting others' work shows dignity of labour.

quiz.q: What happens if workers who repair roads stop working?
options: Roads become damaged and travel becomes hard
quiz.explain: Every job supports daily life; without road workers, roads would fall apart.
quiz.mistake: Does not see how everyday jobs support life

quiz.q: Who among these does work that deserves respect?
quiz.explain: Honest, useful work deserves respect; harmful acts are not honest work.
quiz.mistake: Confuses honest work with harmful acts

teach.ask: Gappu asks, 'Are some jobs better than others? Is a sweeper less important than an engineer?'
teach.praise: You are right! Dignity of labour means every honest job deserves respect. The sweeper and the engineer are both important!
teach.nudge: Should we respect some jobs more than others? What does 'dignity of labour' mean?
